rationale: Final-week Capital Strategic Partners poll (Aug 15, FloridaPolitics) shows Elijah leading Mills 44-27 with 49% already voted; Victory Insights rated CD-7 'Lean Elijah' and both Haridopolos and Luna endorsed Elijah.

Vindman has raised ~$16-19M vs Nixon's ~$1M, runs a large GOTV operation and is the widely expected nominee (Miami Times, Aug 2026), though a July Change Research/D poll had him only 34-24 and Nixon has progressive momentum (Miami Herald, Aug 2).
Wahab led the June 16 top-two primary 42.8%-16.8% over Hernandez in a heavily Democratic district and is a sitting state senator; Polymarket has Wahab ~94% for the Aug 18 runoff.

Axios (Jun 26) shortlisted Overton, Vacirca and Ferrara, with some sources preferring Ferrara, while Kalshi odds (Aug 6) favored Vacirca at ~61% over Overton 25%; the White House may not act before the vote.

No such request has been reported yet; Moody is the only leading with AIPAC backing ($325K plus endorsement) in a competitive race (FundVoter, FloridaPolitics), so she is the most plausible subject of a keep-out request by Aug 25, but the base rate of this event is low.

Former FM Kuleba publicly advocated wartime elections in April 2026 interviews ('I hold that Ukraine needs wartime elections', kurs.if.ua, Apr 14); Tymoshenko and Poroshenko still oppose wartime votes (Interfax, Jan 2026), but an earlier 2025 call could pre-empt the question.

MAGA Inc. has $400M+ but no general-election buy announced (Reuters, Jul 20); a senior White House official said spending decisions needn't be made before the Sept 9 convention (Yahoo). Budgets are likely to be split across NC/OH/ME/TX/MI, so NC is the most common battleground for Senate and House money.

No Republican senator has signaled a Judiciary inquiry into Trump Jr.'s foreign deals; criticism comes mainly from Democrats (Warren/Blumenthal/Kim letters), so this is a low-probability event, and any single named senator is unlikely.

No state AG has announced a settlement with TikTok yet; TikTok recently settled the Kentucky Breathitt County schools Bellwether case (May 2026) and Minnesota's AG case survived dismissal (Mar 2026, ag.state.mn.us), making those states the most plausible, but 14 state suits are still in discovery and a deal by Sept 30 is unlikely.

Florida AG Uthmeier filed the first state-led suit against OpenAI on Jun 1, 2026 and is already seeking an injunction to stop its practices, which is the closest any state is to formally asking a court to halt ChatGPT development.

The draft NPRM circulating (TPM, Aug 11; WIRED, Aug 8) would count only lawful permanent residents, approved asylees and approved refugees, excluding all other foreign-country citizens, so LPR is the most likely descriptive status if it is published by Sept 30.
